content.title: About
content.content: Kiwifruit is the edible berry of the Actinidia deliciosa vine, native to China. The green variety has an oval shape, a thin fuzzy skin, and bright green flesh speckled with tiny black seeds. It is usually eaten raw and added to salads, desserts, and drinks.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Kiwifruit is sometimes called the "Chinese gooseberry" but belongs to the actinidiaceae family.
It contains 2–3 times more vitamin C than an orange.
The enzyme actinidin in kiwifruit helps break down proteins, making it a natural meat tenderizer.
Traditional Chinese medicine has used kiwifruit to aid digestion.
Several cultivars exist, but the green raw fruit is the most widely traded worldwide.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Kiwifruit is one of the richest natural sources of vitamin C, supporting immune function and protecting cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion, helps maintain satiety, and supports gut health.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium aids blood pressure regulation and heart function.

items.title: Contains antioxidants
items.content: Polyphenols and carotenoids in kiwifruit protect cells from free‑radical damage.

items.title: Supports eye health
items.content: Lutein and zeaxanthin contribute to retinal health and may reduce the risk of age‑related macular degeneration.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to kiwifruit, ranging from itching and swelling to severe respiratory symptoms.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Kiwifruit can enhance the effect of certain blood thinners; consult a healthcare professional if you take such medications.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: Its high acidity may irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Kiwifruit is typically eaten fresh: cut in half and scoop out the flesh with a spoon or peel the skin with a knife. It can be added to smoothies, yogurts, salads, desserts, and sauces. For a milder flavor, lightly bake the fruit.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep kiwifruit at room temperature until ripe (about 3–5 days). Once ripe, store them in the refrigerator’s fruit drawer, where they stay fresh for up to a week. Avoid storing near other fruits, as kiwifruit emit ethylene, which speeds up ripening.
